candidates.name: Akkas-Syria Gas Pipeline
candidates.monitor_reason: Fails add-threshold leg (c) concrete step (and arguably (a) sponsor). The Akkas-to-Syria/AGP gas EXPORT pipeline has no MOU, tender, FEED, EPC award, permit, or FID of its own — it exists only as a long-standing aspiration (2004 Egypt/Jordan/Syria/Lebanon framework to connect AGP to Iraq's grid; ~2009 Akkas–Europe-via-Türkiye concept) that stalled in the Syrian war / ISIS's 2014 seizure of Akkas, and is now only under 'renewed discussion' post-Assad. All concrete 2025-26 activity attaches to the Akkas FIELD (SLB drilling Jan 2026; Midland Oil Company lead; earlier Ukrzemresurs/KOGAS-Daewoo contracts), whose gas is targeted at domestic power generation, not a cross-border export line.
candidates.researcher_notes: Match-to-existing re-checked and ruled out: distinct from P0450 (Iran–Iraq–Syria/'Friendship', Iranian gas Asaluyeh→Damascus, cancelled), P1841 (Baiji-K3-Al Kaem, terminates at Al-Qa'im INSIDE Iraq, operating), and P7460/P7466/P7467 (Okaz–Al-Anbar, domestic Okaz-field feed to Anbar power plant, proposed). No existing GEM gas row captures an Akkas→Syria→AGP cross-border export link. However it does not clear the Discovery add-threshold. Add-threshold assessment: (a) sponsor — NOT identified for the pipeline itself (SLB/Midland Oil Company/Ukrzemresurs/KOGAS are Akkas FIELD operators, not pipeline sponsors); (b) endpoints — roughly present (Akkas, al-Anbar, ~30 km S of Al-Qa'im on the Syrian border → Syria → Arab Gas Pipeline toward Türkiye/Europe); (c) concrete step — ABSENT: no MOU/tender/FEED/EPC/permit/FID for the export pipeline. Sources: karamshaar.com AGP/Syria analysis (Jan 2026, explicitly frames Akkas→AGP as historical/aspirational, halted by war, only under renewed post-Assad discussion) and en.wikipedia Arab_Gas_Pipeline (2004 four-country framework to link AGP with Iraq's grid) — both URL-verified (200 + expected substring). Corroborated independently by Energy Intelligence and OilPrice coverage of the Akkas field (domestic-supply focus; SLB drilling started Jan 2026). Note the recent concrete Iraq–Syria cross-border activity is a different project and a different commodity: the Kirkuk–Baniyas OIL pipeline revival (oil, not gas). Confidence: findings well-supported by 2+ independent English sources, but the pipeline itself remains rumor/aspiration — low tier as an early-stage monitor item. Recommend keeping on the watchlist; revisit if a cross-border gas MOU/tender/EPC or a formal Iraq–Syria gas-transit agreement is signed.

candidates.name: Al-Faw Grand Port LNG-Abu Ghraib Supply Pipeline
candidates.monitor_reason: Add-threshold leg (b) fails: endpoints/route indeterminate. The '130 km connecting pipeline' has contradictory, physically impossible endpoints across sources ('130 km pipeline from Al-Faw port' per emilecon vs '130km at Abu Ghraib' per PM readout/MEED/Goalfore) — Al-Faw port to Abu Ghraib is ~550 km, so a 130 km line cannot connect them, making the route unstageable. Corroboration also fails the 2+ independent test: all figures trace to one 26 Aug 2025 cabinet press readout (PM media office) reprinted by English trade press.
candidates.researcher_notes:
SKEPTICAL VERDICT: monitor, not new_row. Match-to-existing re-checked against all 54 Iraq gas rows in discovery_context.json — no existing row is this LNG-import connecting pipeline (P7435 Khor Al-Zubair FSRU tie-in is a separate completed 40 km/42in line; P7434 Mahmudiyah-Besmaya is a distinct grid segment; P5857 Zubair-Faw is a shelved 18in/105km line in the opposite delivery direction; the 45 km Mahmudiyah-Abu Ghraib PS line reported completed June 2025 is a grid feeder, not this LNG trunk). Confirmed the consolidator's finding that no roster line runs north from Al-Faw port.

WHAT IS CONFIRMED: Iraq's Cabinet approved a >10,000 MW power package on 26 Aug 2025 (per PM media office) that bundles LNG reception infrastructure at Al-Faw Grand Port — jetty + FSRU + 'connecting pipelines: 17 km at Al-Faw and 130 km at Abu Ghraib' — feeding 3,000 MW CCGT plants at Al-Faw (developer Superior Technology Systems, UAE) and Abu Ghraib (developer Emirate Technology Company), each ~400 MMscf/d imported LNG, 25-yr BOO, GE Vernova technology. The FSRU itself was later awarded to Excelerate Energy (~$450M). Concrete step (leg c) IS met (cabinet approval).

WHY IT FAILS AS A STAGEABLE ROW: (1) Corroboration — verified both English evidence URLs (url_verifier OK, 200 + content), but MEED/Goalfore/Emilecon all reprint the SAME 26 Aug 2025 cabinet readout; not 2+ independent sources. In-country Arabic reporting closest to primary (attaqa.net, 16 Aug 2025) does NOT mention any 130 km line — it describes different, already-completed pipelines (40 km Khor Al-Zubair-Shatt Al-Arab by South Gas Co./Petroproject = existing P7435; 45 km Mahmudiyah-Abu Ghraib PS by Petroproject) and reports the FSRU still at the bid stage (6 firms invited, 2 qualified, pending Diwani Order Committee). (2) Endpoints/route — the '130 km' figure is internally contradictory (emilecon: 'from Al-Faw port'; PM/MEED: 'at Abu Ghraib') and physically impossible for an Al-Faw->Abu Ghraib connection (~550 km apart), so no coherent route or endpoints can be established; the consolidator's 'port-to-national-grid trunk' reading is unsourced inference. (3) No distinct pipeline sponsor — the connecting pipelines are an unattributed bundled component of the LNG import/IPP package, not a separately identified project.

RECOMMENDATION: Monitor. Re-check when the FSRU/import scheme reaches FEED/EPC award for the connecting pipeline specifically, or when a source gives a coherent, corroborated route (from/to + length). Confidence tier low; single reprinted primary source.

candidates.name: Chemchemal-Bazian Gas Pipeline

values.RouteNotes: Announced as a dedicated 40 km line from the Chemchemal field to industrial consumers in the Bazian area; no published GIS route. To be built by (unnamed) private-sector companies.

candidates.researcher_notes:
NEW ROW. Passes all three add-threshold legs: (a) sponsor = Pearl Petroleum consortium (Dana Gas + Crescent Petroleum operating) developing the Chemchemal field under a KRG concession; (b) country + endpoints = Iraq, Chemchemal field (Sulaymaniyah) -> Bazian industrial area; (c) concrete step = 10-year Gas Sales Agreements signed Jan 2026 with Bazian-area offtakers (Mass/Bazian/Delta/Gasin/Sulaimani Cement), $160m committed to field development, first gas targeted H2 2027. Corroborated by >=2 independent sources: Crescent Petroleum press release (operator/primary), World Oil (independent trade press), OilPrice analysis, and Iraqi News all confirm a 'dedicated 40 km pipeline' from Chemchemal to Bazian industrial consumers, privately funded, deliveries from H2 2027. All four URLs passed url_verifier (200 + expected content). Confidence: HIGH on existence, endpoints, 40 km length, sponsor, and the Jan-2026 GSA milestone.

MATCH CHECK: Distinct from existing GEM rows. P6823 (Khormor-Pirdawood PP) and P4047 (Khormor-Erbil, construction) are Khor Mor-sourced lines feeding power plants / Erbil; this is a Chemchemal-field-sourced, privately built line to Bazian INDUSTRIAL (cement) consumers. No roster row originates at Chemchemal. Not a duplicate.

DELIBERATE OMISSIONS (skeptical calls): (1) Capacity LEFT BLANK. The widely cited '142 MMscf/d' is the FIELD-WIDE GSA offtake total across ALL new industrial customers (both the Bazian cement cluster AND the separate Erbil line to Van Steel), per World Oil ('up to 142 MMscf/d collectively across all industrial customers'). Assigning the full 142 MMscf/d to the Bazian line alone would overstate it; sources do not disaggregate a per-line rating. (2) Owner LEFT BLANK. Sources say the pipeline is 'to be built by private-sector companies' but name no specific builder/owner entity; did not run/stage a new owner entity. (3) $160m cost NOT attributed to the pipeline — it covers three wells + an extended well test facility + enabling infrastructure for the whole field program, not the pipeline specifically. (4) FIDStatus blank — GSAs are offtake agreements, not a pipeline construction FID. (5) No published GIS route -> RouteAccuracy 'no route'. Sibling candidate 'chemchemal-erbil-industrial-gas' is a separate build (Van Steel offtaker) and is vetted separately.

candidates.name: Chemchemal-Erbil industrial gas supply pipeline
candidates.monitor_reason: Fails add-threshold legs (a) and (b). (a) No identified sponsor: the only wording anywhere is 'new pipelines are to be built by private-sector companies' -- the companies are unnamed; Pearl Petroleum (Dana Gas/Crescent) is the gas seller under the GSA, not stated as the pipeline builder. (b) Endpoints not established: the delivery point is Van Steel Company in Erbil governorate, but no source gives an origin, route, length, or diameter -- 'Chemchemal-Erbil' is an inferred name, and it is equally plausible the Erbil supply arrives as a tie-in/spur off the existing Khor Mor-Erbil corridor (GEM P4047, 36-in, construction) rather than a standalone Chemchemal-Erbil trunk. (c) is only partially met: the 10-year GSA with Van Steel (signed Jan 2026, first gas H2 2027) is a concrete commercial step for the gas supply, but there is no tender, FEED, or EPC award for the pipeline itself. Contrast: the sibling Bazian line IS specified (dedicated 40 km, Chemchemal field direct to Bazian) in the same release, showing the sponsors describe pipelines concretely when they exist as defined projects -- the Erbil leg deliberately is not.
candidates.researcher_notes: Vetted 2026-07-04 (CB). Sole primary source is the 26 Jan 2026 Dana Gas/Crescent Petroleum (Pearl Petroleum) press release announcing 142 MMscf/d of 10-year GSAs from the Chemchemal field, with first gas H2 2027; Van Steel Company (Erbil governorate) is the sole Erbil offtaker named. On the pipeline serving Erbil the release says only that 'new pipelines are to be built by private-sector companies to supply gas to industrial users in Erbil and Bazian' -- no builder, origin, route, length, diameter, cost, or schedule. All other coverage checked (World Oil, Iraqi News, Egypt Oil & Gas, Sharjah24, MEES, Rudaw) reprints the same release; zero independent corroboration of a distinct Erbil pipeline project, so tier = low / independent = false. Match-to-existing re-checked against the 54-row Iraq gas roster: not the same project as P4047 Khormor-Erbil Gas Pipeline (that is the Khor Mor-to-Erbil power corridor, already under construction pre-dating this GSA) and not P4053 Erbil-Duhok; but a tie-in delivering Chemchemal gas to Van Steel via the P4047 corridor cannot be ruled out -- if that materializes, the correct treatment is likely a note/spur on P4047, not a new row. Re-vet when a builder is named, an origin/route is disclosed, or a pipeline tender/EPC award appears (watch Dana Gas/Crescent releases and KRG MNR through 2026-2027 ahead of H2 2027 first gas). The two cited URLs passed scripts/url_verifier.py on 2026-07-04 (the rudaw.net/business/26012026-amp URL was dropped -- it 200s to a nav shell without the article text and failed verification). The concrete sibling (dedicated 40 km Chemchemal-Bazian line) is handled under its own candidate slug.

candidates.name: Diyala Gas Fields Supply Pipeline (Gilabat-Qumar / Khashim Ahmer-Injana)
candidates.monitor_reason: Fails add-threshold leg (c) as applied to a pipeline, and (b) is only partial. The concrete steps on record (20-year development contracts signed Feb 2023 and activated Oct-Dec 2023; 3D seismic phase 1 completed Apr 2025) are FIELD-development milestones, not a pipeline-specific step (no pipeline tender / FEED / EPC / route / FID). No distinct transmission pipeline is defined anywhere: the primary source commits only to generic 'pipelines and infrastructure to supply gas' to 'nearby power plants' with no route, length, diameter, or named endpoints, so it cannot be confirmed to be a distinct transmission line rather than field/plant-boundary supply infrastructure. Project is still in appraisal (seismic), and the 'first gas within 18 months' (mid-2024) target has slipped past April 2025.
candidates.researcher_notes: SPONSOR (leg a) MET: Crescent Petroleum (UAE; Crescent won these blocks in the 2018 5th licensing round, contracts re-signed/activated 2023). ENDPOINTS (leg b) PARTIAL: source = Gilabat-Qumar and Khashim Ahmer-Injana gas fields, Diyala Province; destination = 'nearby power plants' -- trade press (Petroleum Economist, 2024) names Mansuriyah power plant, ramping 120 -> up to 520 MMscfd feeding Mansuriyah plus other nearby Diyala stations. No pipeline route/length/diameter is published. VOLUMES are field production (initially 250 MMscfd, up to ~520 MMscfd), NOT a verified single-pipeline throughput. CONCRETE STEP (leg c) is field-level only. MATCH-TO-EXISTING re-checked against all 54 Iraq gas rows: no existing row covers a Crescent new-build from these Diyala fields. P4058 'Eastern Iraq Gas Pipeline' (operating, cap 350) is the pre-existing Iranian import corridor into Diyala/Baghdad, NOT this build -- not a match. CONFIDENCE: medium. Corroboration: Crescent primary PR (2023-02) + Argus (independent, 2023-02) + Crescent seismic PR (2025-04); Zawya is a reprint of the Crescent PR and does not count as independent. All four cited URLs verified HTTP 200 via url_verifier.py. RECOMMENDATION: monitor for a pipeline-specific milestone (defined route/endpoints, pipeline EPC/tender, or FID) before staging a new_row; re-check on the next annual pass given the field development is active.

candidates.researcher_notes: NEW ROW. Confirmed distinct from the two existing Halfaya-area gas rows: P6832 (Bazargan-Halfaya, 18in, INBOUND sour gas from the Iran-border Buzurgan complex into Halfaya) and P4058 (Eastern Iraq Gas Pipeline, 48in / 350 capacity) — neither matches this 24in / 21km OUTBOUND dry-gas outlet, and endpoints/diameter rule out corridor overlap with P4058. Add-threshold met on all three legs: (a) sponsor = PetroChina Halfaya operating consortium (field operator; built by China Petroleum Pipeline Company / CPECC, a CNPC subsidiary); (b) endpoints = Halfaya oil field -> Al-Kahla power station, Maysan governorate; (c) concrete step = operating (commissioned early 2013). EXISTENCE + STATUS = high confidence (independent: Iraq Oil Report 2013 EN, Zawya 2023 EN, Al Jazeera 2024 AR, NS Energy/TotalEnergies for the operator consortium). SPEC (24in diameter, 21km length, 40 MMcf/d initial pilot flow) rests primarily on the Iraq Oil Report Feb-2013 report, a reputable specialist source, but is effectively single-sourced for the exact figures -> overall tier MEDIUM. Capacity left BLANK: the only figure available is the 40 MMcf/d 2013 pilot flow, which is a throughput at start-up, not a stated design capacity, and is now outdated (the 300 MMscf/d Halfaya GPP came online 2023-2024). Owner/Parent reflect the Halfaya field service-contract consortium (PetroChina Halfaya 37.5% operator; TotalEnergies 18.75%; Petronas Carigali 18.75%; Missan Oil Company 25%) per NS Energy / TotalEnergies; note the asset is legally state-owned under Iraq's technical service contract, and Missan Oil Company operates the processing complexes (Arabic sources, June 2026). EndLocation set to Al-Kahla power station (the documented terminus of this 24in line); the Halfaya GPP's dry gas also feeds the Amara and Maysan power plants (Zawya/Al Jazeera 2023-2024), but that later delivery may run on additional/separate lines and is NOT conflated into this row's spec. mubasher.info Arabic article on the Kahla gas-connection line opening exists but repeatedly timed out in url_verifier, so it was NOT cited. No fabricated URLs; all cited URLs passed url_verifier. Route: no official GIS geometry located; not staged (geometry -> routes repo).

candidates.name: Iraq-Jordan Gas Pipeline (Basra-Aqaba gas leg)

values.OtherEnglishNames: Iraq-Jordan Gas Pipeline; Basra-Aqaba twin pipeline (gas component); Rumaila-Aqaba gas pipeline

candidates.researcher_notes: MATCH CHECK: No Jordan-touching or Basra-Aqaba gas row exists in the 54-row Iraq gas roster (nearest are P7573 Basra-Ceyhan, to Turkey, and P0450 Iran-Iraq-Syria) so this is not an existing GEM gas row. The oil leg is tracked separately in GOIT (gem.wiki 'Basra-Aqaba Oil Pipeline'); this candidate is the distinct GGIT gas leg. ADD-THRESHOLD (all three met): (a) sponsor = Iraq Ministry of Oil + Jordan Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources (state-to-state); (b) endpoints = Basra, Iraq -> Aqaba, Jordan; (c) concrete step = April 2013 intergovernmental agreement / framework for an ~$18bn TWIN oil-AND-gas pipeline, with Jordan's cabinet approving construction (2013) and Iraq's cabinet re-approving the twin oil+gas project in Feb 2018. CONFIRMED DATA: parallel gas line rated 350 MMcf/d within Iraq and 258 MMcf/d on the Jordanian stretch (258 used as Capacity value); twin-corridor length 1,680 km (~1,044 mi) — the gas line runs parallel to the oil line in the same corridor, so LengthKnown reflects the shared corridor length (no separate gas-only geometry published). Diameter, Owner, and a gas-specific cost were never disclosed (the $18bn was the combined twin figure) so left blank. STATUS = cancelled: the gas component was dropped in the 2017 downscoping to reduce cost and expedite the oil-only line (corroborated across AGSI and thenewregion analyses seen in search, and consistent with Bayan Center 2020 which reports only 'the oil pipeline project is continuing'); the gas leg was briefly revived in the Feb 2018 twin re-approval (Rudaw) but the project ultimately proceeded oil-only. GEM does track cancelled cross-border proposals (cf. P0450, P0481). CONFIDENCE: high — >=2 independent English outlets (UPI 2013, Pipeline Technology Journal, MEED, Rudaw 2018, Bayan Center 2020) agree on sponsors, endpoints, 258 MMcf/d gas, and 1,680 km, and are not reprints of one wire. ROUTE: no official GIS route for the gas line; Basra->Aqaba corridor only (route work out of scope, geometry belongs to the routes repo). Recommend ShelvedCancelledType handled at apply time (confirmed cancellation, not presumed).

candidates.name: Miran gas field export pipeline (to Bazian power plant)

candidates.researcher_notes: Match-to-existing re-checked independently against all 54 Iraq gas rows in discovery_context.json: no Miran- or Bazian-destination pipeline exists (nearest Kurdistan gas lines P6823 Khormor-Pirdawood, P4047 Khormor-Erbil, P7457 Semel-Duhok are distinct) - not matched_existing.
